subject: Seat-scarcity: Skyforge co-sell sequencing and account slot assignment
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T16:12:00Z
Subject: Seat-scarcity: Skyforge co-sell sequencing and account slot assignment

Team —

Quick primer: Skyforge (ISV) has requested co-sell seats for a formal integration push. Their pipeline shows a cluster of mid-market targets where channel overlap with our account teams is likely. Given limited partner slot capacity for Q3 (we've already allocated ~70% to strategic ISVs), I sketched a pragmatic slotting approach and attached a working "slotting_matrix.xlsx".

High-level proposal (please review inline in the matrix):
- Slot types: Strategic (A) / Growth (B) / Trial (C) — cap Strategic seats = 6, Growth = 12, Trial = 20 (subject to legal/commercial)
- Allocation rules: first engagement + co-sell playbook match earns provisional seat; seat held for 30 days pending pipeline activity
- Escalation: disputed accounts should route to Partner Ops (Marissa) who will adjudicate within 3 business days
- Exceptions: regulated verticals (healthcare/finserv) require explicit approval from Security/Compliance and are default-excluded

Asks:
1) Marissa — can you run the matrix against the hot account list and flag any collisions with existing co-sell commitments?
2) Karthik — can you propose routing logic for requests that come through the marketplace vs. direct partner rep?
3) Soojin — any upfront limits you want for enablement capacity (training seats, demo credits)?

I want to finalize internal policy and get a one-page MOU out to Skyforge by EOD Wednesday so the partner can start account outreach next week.

Attachments: slotting_matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Head of Partner GTM, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Seat-scarcity: Skyforge co-sell sequencing and account slot assignment

Jasmine —

Thanks for the draft. I ran the slotting matrix against our active co-sell roster and attached a short list (priority_accounts.csv) with collisions and recommended holds. Quick notes: 
- Reduce Strategic cap from 6 -> 5; one of the Strategic accounts is already under an exclusivity test with NovaEdge.
- Please mark any account with existing compliance reviews as "requires-sg" so legal sees them up front.
- Recommend a soft-lock of 48 hours when two internal teams claim the same seat; that buys Partner Ops time to resolve.

I added inline comments to the matrix and flagged a handful of accounts I think Skyforge should not pursue (regulated healthcare and banking customers).

Marissa

Folks —

Quick routing suggestions based on expected request sources:

1) Marketplace RFCs (automated):
   - If Skyforge opens a marketplace request, auto-create provisional seat and require evidence of 2 meetings within 21 days. If not met, seat is released automatically.
2) Partner rep direct outreach:
   - Partner rep claims -> Partner Ops (Marissa) verifies conflict -> if no conflict, seat confirmed for 30 days.
3) Inside-sales conflict:
   - If inside-sales already has a cover (meeting count >=3), block seat and open escalation for a co-sell carve-out (Partner/Sales leadership to decide).

Operational controls:
- Metric: seat utilization % by partner — aim >= 60% for Growth seats; if below 40% for two consecutive months, reclaim.
- Reserve pool: Hold 15% of total slots as "strategic reserve" for exec-sponsored plays (we can bump up to 20% for FY28 Q3).

Happy to model the routing rules for the console if folks agree to these guardrails.

Karthik
Head of Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
